Requirements are equally met: both decks show Resilient $440k/$155k, 2.8yr and $25k on slides 1 and 8 (A1,A8; B1,B8), correct M1-M6 actual/target and 5,150/5,670/520 totals on slide 2 (A2; B2), complete option and site tables with South constrained (A3,A5; B3,B5), correct 124/155/186 scenarios with 3.5/2.8/2.4yr and -68/25/118 on slide 4 (A4; B4), two-lane week-10 gate roadmap (A6; B6), correctly placed R1-R5 with all mitigations (A7; B7), and all three gate thresholds with HOLD (A8; B8). Requirements are materially identical: both show Resilient/$440k/$155k/2.8yr/+$25k on slide 1 (A1,B1), correct M1-M6 actual/target and 5630/5960/-330 on slide 2 (A2,B2), full option cells on slide 3 (A3,B3), 124/155/186 with 3.5/2.8/2.4yr and -68/25/118 on slide 4 (A4,B4), full five-site cells, 1700/1660 and North/Central/West constrained on slide 5 (A5,B5), separated lanes with Validate AND Train to Week 10 gate and Weeks 11-14 rollout on slide 6 (A6,B6), R1-R5 at correct coordinates with all mitigations on slide 7 (A7,B7), and three gate thresholds plus HOLD on slide 8 (A8,B8); both also omit an explicit $155k annual saving on slide 8. Both decks use the same layouts, charts, tables and roadmap/risk visuals, and both satisfy the visible requirements: e.g. A slides 1/8 and B slides 1/8 recommend Resilient at $440k/$155k with 2.8-year payback; A slide 2 and B slide 2 show M4 actual 1150, all other actual/target values and totals 5630/5960/gap 330; A slides 3-5 and B slides 3-5 preserve all option and site cells, scenario savings 124/155/186, paybacks 3.5/2.8/2.4 and nets -68/25/118, and totals 1700/1660; A slides 6-7 and B slides 6-7 show separated lanes, unchanged timings, Validate AND Train to a week-10 gate, and R1-R5 at correct coordinates with mitigations; A slide 8 and B slide 8 state >=99.5%, >=95% for all five sites, backup-power passed and HOLD. Requirements are closely matched: both decks recommend Resilient with $440k/$155k and 2.8-year payback on slides 1 and 8, preserve M1-M6 actual/target values and 5,150/5,670/520 totals on slide 2, show all option and site table cells on slides 3 and 5, and show 124/155/186 savings with 3.5/2.8/2.4-year paybacks and -68/25/118 nets on slide 4. Deck B wins because it meets the risk-matrix requirement correctly and has no visible layout defects, while Deck A has two clear faults. On the other slides both decks cover the same facts: Resilient at $440k, $155k/yr, 2.8 years and $25k on slides 1 and 8; M4 at 1150 with totals 5630/5960/330 on slide 2; the full option table on slide 3; 124/155/186 with 3.5/2.8/2.4 and -68/25/118 on slide 4; all five site rows with North, Central and West constrained on slide 5; the two-lane roadmap with the Week 10 gate and Weeks 11-14 rollout on slide 6; and the three thresholds with HOLD on slide 8. The two decks share the same layout, data and storyline, so the differences are small. Both meet the key requirements: exactly eight slides with no cover-only slide; Resilient recommended with $440k, $155k/yr, 2.8 yrs and $25k on slide 1 (A1, B1); M4 actual shown as 1080 and all totals 5150/5670/520 (A2, B2); the full option table (A3, B3); the 124/155/186 chart with 3.5/2.8/2.4 paybacks and −68/25/118 nets (A4, B4); every five-site cell, the 1600/1710 totals and South flagged as constrained (A5, B5); Technical and People lanes with Validate AND Train both feeding the week-10 gate and rollout in weeks 11–14 (A6, B6); R1–R5 at their correct coordinates with all mitigations (A7, B7); and all three gate thresholds plus HOLD (A8, B8). B is slightly cleaner on legibility. A1's KPI label 'Three-year net (3 × 155 − 440)' wraps awkwardly, while B1's is compact. A slide 7 swaps the axes, labelling the vertical axis 'Likelihood 1-5' and the horizontal axis 'Impact 1-5'. Its tick numbers are also misaligned: the 5-1 labels are crowded beside the top rows, and the 1-5 labels are offset from the columns. A reader can still decode the positions through the side table, but the visual is confusing. B slide 7 uses likelihood across and impact upward, with R1 (L4, I3), R2 (L2, I5), R3 (L3, I4), R4 (L2, I2) and R5 (L3, I5) all in the right cells, plus a complete mitigations table. On design and legibility, A's titles wrap to two lines on slides 3-8, and A leaves large empty areas in slide 1's 'Why Resilient' box, slide 3's tradeoff box and slide 8's GO/HOLD cards. B keeps one-line titles on all eight slides, uses consistent cards and slide numbers, and shows large KPI numbers on slides 1 and 2. B also adds useful findings that follow from the supplied data: slide 5 notes that Central, South and East are below the 95% gate, and slide 8 links those gaps to the HOLD risk. A has its own strengths: slide 3 explains the tradeoff against both Lean and Balanced, slide 4 shows saving values in its table, and slide 6 labels each roadmap dependency explicitly. B has minor flaws: the 910 label sits close to the bar on slide 2, slide 3 compares only against Balanced, and slide 8's bottom note crowds the footer. A's added detail does not outweigh its axis error and weaker layout.

Both decks satisfy the visible requirements and communicate the same complete decision story. Both decks cover the same eight-slide story with correct core numbers: 440/155/2.8/25 on slides 1 and 8, M4=1150, totals 5630/5960/330, scenarios 124/155/186 with 3.5/2.8/2.4 and -68/25/118, North/Central/West constrained, gate Week 10 and rollout Weeks 11-14. The deciding difference is the risk matrix. In Deck A slide 7 the axis labels do not line up with the grid: the Impact labels 5-1 sit between rows, R2 and R5 are drawn above the row labelled 5, R1 sits near likelihood 4.5, and R4 sits near impact 1. Each deck has one visible requirement miss, so A wins on design, legibility and visual communication rather than on compliance. Requirements: Both decks show the core facts correctly. Both recommend Resilient on slides 1 and 8 and show the M4 actual of 1150 with the unchanged targets and the 5630/5960/330 totals on slide 2. Both show all option cells on slide 3, the 124/155/186 scenarios with 3.5/2.8/2.4 paybacks and -68/25/118 nets on slide 4, and the full site table with North, Central and West constrained on slide 5. Both show week-10 gate and weeks 11-14 rollout on slides 6 and 8, R5 at likelihood 3 / impact 5 with all mitigations on slide 7, and the three thresholds plus HOLD on slide 8. A's miss: slide 8 omits the $155k annual saving; it shows only the $440k investment, the 2.8-year payback and the $25k net. B's miss: slide 7 puts likelihood on the vertical axis and impact on the horizontal, against card 2's 'likelihood on x, impact on y'. The points are consistent with B's swapped axes, but the spec is not followed. A's slide 7 follows the specified axes with correct coordinates. B also makes small claims the data does not support: slide 6's title says 'build and train converge' when it is Validate and Train, and slide 4 says downside risk is 'bounded at −$68k'. Requirements are therefore a tie. Design: A uses consistent metric cards, tables and callouts (A1, A3, A5, A8) with balanced layouts. B relies on large rounded boxes with a lot of empty interior space (B5 totals and constrained boxes, B7 mitigation panel, B8 gate box). Legibility: B7's vertically stacked 'L-i-k-e-l-i-h-o-o-d' label is hard to read, and B2's data footnote crowds the footer. A's text is smaller in places but clean at this resolution. Visual communication: A adds analytic cues that support the decision. These include gap/day and status columns (A5), payback and 3-year net columns in the option table (A3), a break-even callout (A4) and a gate status-today column (A8). B mostly restates the data. Coherence: both follow the eight-step story with finding titles and consistent footers. A ties the narrative together more tightly, with on-time exposure on A5 linking to the gate status on A8, but this is not enough to call it a meaningful gap. Overall: requirements are even, and A's stronger design, legibility and visual communication decide it.

A's design and communication advantage outweighs B's risk-axis-orientation advantage.

Deck B is more polished, legible and coherent at this resolution: consistent headers, footers and slide numbers 01/08-08/08 (B1-B8), clean charts/tables (B2-B5), a clear two-lane connected roadmap (B6) and an unambiguous GO/HOLD gate layout (B8). Tradeoff: Deck B is more consistently designed and legible across all 8 slides, with clean KPI cards on B1, intact table headers on B3/B5, consistent footers and page numbers, and orthogonal roadmap connectors on B6; Deck A has the broken 'Demand/da y'/'Capacity/d ay' headers on A5 and messier diagonal connectors on A6. Both decks satisfy the same eight-slide requirements with identical core data, including Resilient $440k/$155k on Slides 1 and 8 (A1/A8 and B1/B8), corrected M4 1,080 and 5,150 vs 5,670 totals on Slide 2 (A2/B2), complete option, scenario, site and risk tables on Slides 3-5 and 7 (A3-A5/A7 and B3-B5/B7), and the week-10 gate with week 11-14 rollout on Slides 6 and 8 (A6/A8 and B6/B8). Both decks visibly satisfy the task’s substantive requirements: A2/B2 preserve monthly values and totals, A3/B3 retain option data, A4/B4 show correct scenarios, and A6/B6 and A8/B8 preserve dependencies, timing and gate conditions. The two decks are nearly identical: same eight-slide story, same data and same layouts. Slides 1-6 and 8 meet the requirements in both. Both decks cover the same eight-slide story and meet nearly all requirements. Deck A wins on cleaner execution and stronger visuals.
